Resolves #21286
🌿 The clone section can no longer promise an agent everything and leave it blind to the running app.

CONTRIBUTING's "Set up the engine from a clone" gains a step that registers the `neo-neural-link` npm package with Claude Code or Codex in one command, names the example that connects already and the config line any other app needs, and moves the link off a taken port. The agent section (`CONTRIBUTING.md:209`) and `.github/AI_QUICK_START.md:5` name the package instead of a Brain checkout, and the Quick Start no longer says Claude Desktop and Claude Code share one MCP configuration file.

Evidence: L3 (a fresh shallow clone of `dev` at `c722f02bad`, registered through the real `claude` and `codex` CLIs, one tool call answered by the running example) → L3 required (#21286 AC-1, AC-2). Residual: none.

Micro-review eligible: docs — pure documentation with no runtime impact, so the cross-family micro-change exception applies.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Proof |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | Outside CI, Test Evidence below: `claude mcp list` reports the registered entry `✔ Connected`, and `get_component_tree` through that entry answers with the example's tree. |

Not measured: a tool call from a Codex agent turn, which needs a signed-in Codex; the scratch home has none, and this machine's Codex homes belong to live maintainer seats. Server and Bridge are the ones AC-1 measured. |
| AC-3 | `CONTRIBUTING.md:209` and `.github/AI_QUICK_START.md:5` name `neo-neural-link`. The Quick Start's Brain-checkout entries stay as the Agent OS setup; its new line 5 sends a reader who only wants the Neural Link to the package. |
| AC-4 | `git grep -n -i -E "share a single MCP\|configures the other" -- '*.md'`: no match. |

## Deltas from ticket
- One command per harness instead of a hand-written entry. `claude mcp add` registers for this clone only, and `codex mcp add` writes exactly the `[mcp_servers.neural-link]` entry the ticket named. A hand-written root `.mcp.json` is neither tracked nor ignored in this repository, so it would sit in `git status` and could ride into a contributor's pull request.
- The ticket's Out of Scope config writer (shared with create-app) is retired, not deferred: each harness's own `mcp add` is that command.
- The port paragraph puts the name before `-e`. `-e` takes several values, so `claude mcp add -e NEO_NL_PORT=8197 neural-link …` fails ("Invalid environment variable format: neural-link"). The name-first form wrote `"env":{"NEO_NL_PORT":"8197"}`, and the Bridge bound 8197 although the shell exported 8198.

## Test Evidence
On a fresh clone, every command under `env -i` with a scratch `HOME` (no maintainer variables):

```text
git clone --depth 1 --branch dev https://github.com/neomjs/neo.git     # c722f02bad
npm install; npm run bundle-browser-deps; npm run build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all   # 34 s
claude mcp add neural-link -- npx -y neo-neural-link
claude mcp list   → neural-link: npx -y neo-neural-link - ✔ Connected
codex mcp add neural-link -- npx -y neo-neural-link
codex mcp list    → neural-link  npx  -y neo-neural-link  -  -  enabled
```

The tool call: a stdio MCP client spawned the entry `claude mcp add` stored (`{"command":"npx","args":["-y","neo-neural-link"]}`). Server `neo-neural-link 1.0.0`, 60 tools; `/examples/button/base/` open headless ("Neo Button"); `get_component_tree` answered on the third poll:

```text
{"tree": {"className": "Neo.examples.button.base.MainContainer", "id": "neo-configuration-viewport-1", "items": [{"className": "Neo.container.Base", "id": "neo-container-1", …
```

38 components. Conditions specific to this machine: port 8081 belongs to the maintainers' own Bridge, so the Bridge ran on 8197 and the scratch clone's example pointed `neuralLinkUrl` there; the dev server ran on `PORT=8095` without `--open`. The call came from an MCP client rather than a Claude Code agent turn, which needs a signed-in account; this machine's runs under the maintainers' settings and hooks.

Change class: zero-delta (`docs`). `agent-preflight` is not hosted here; `check-relative-links` and `check-engine-brain-boundary` pass locally.

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — contributor setup prose in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `.github/AI_QUICK_START.md`. There is no runtime surface, no consumed contract and no architectural concept to teach.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim: a clone's agent gets the Neural Link from the `neo-neural-link` npm package with one `mcp add` per harness, and the Quick Start stops saying that Claude Desktop and Claude Code share one MCP file. I checked it at the exact head `aa433f7b54`:
- `examples/button/base/neo-config.json` sets `useAiClient: true`.
- `#set-up-the-engine-from-a-clone` resolves to `CONTRIBUTING.md:14`, and the promise at `:200`, "Your agent needs nothing beyond the clone above", now holds.
- `npm view neo-neural-link` gives 1.0.0, with bin `ai/mcp/server/neural-link/standalone.mjs`.
- Against the installed CLIs (Claude Code 2.1.212, Codex):
  - `claude mcp add` defaults to `--scope local`, so "for this clone" is right.
  - Its `-e, --env <env...>` is variadic, which is why the name must come first, as the Deltas say.
  - `codex mcp add` takes `--env <KEY=VALUE>`, and `claude mcp add-from-claude-desktop` exists.

AC-1's call through the stored entry is a real receipt, and AC-2 names why the Codex agent turn was not measured. CI is green.

I looked for three gaps and found none: a sentence still claiming one shared file (AC-4's grep), a Brain checkout still required for the link (the new Quick Start line routes around it), and a port that disagrees with `neuralLinkUrl`'s default (8081 in both).

One optional nit, not an action: `claude mcp add-from-claude-desktop --help` says "(Mac and WSL only)". The Quick Start sentence that names it sits right above a Windows path, so a native Windows reader may try it. "(macOS and WSL)" would close that.

**Findings:** None. No required actions — eligible for human merge.
